desc: Prove fixed-target feasibility is exactly \(M(S)\ge m-x\), with \(S\) at least every fixed A/B value, where \(M(S)=\sum_b\min(\mathrm{countB}[b],\mathrm{countA}[S-b])\).
Prove that if \(m>x\), any feasible target is a fixed-A plus fixed-B sum, while if \(m\le x\), a sufficiently large target always works.
Implement the stdin/stdout Python solution using frequency maps and \(O(D_A D_B)\) candidate-sum aggregation.
Validate edge cases: all unknown values, only one array containing unknowns, repeated fixed values, no unknowns, and large target sums.
